items.headline: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
items.blurb: The left-wing incumbent president had lost the first round to right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.
items.text: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting. Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy". Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election. Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same. Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula's lawyer and alleging bias. But both teams had requested an extension to voting times - Lula's had argued that voters in São Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling

items.headline: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, ending England’s 25-year wait
items.blurb: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has won his first Ballon d’Or after a record-breaking season.
items.text: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has won his first Ballon d’Or after a record-breaking season, becoming the first Englishman to claim football’s top individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane scored 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season.

A year after the fall of El Fasher , the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city. A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze . The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”. items.text: Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. "We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday. Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Celebrations erupted after Vučić conceded. Vučić called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence. items.text: Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety. Is it a deliberate military strategy? T he water was rising rapidly. It had already reached Cayni Ali’s waist. Her home, five metres from the flooded River Juba in southern Somalia , never stood a chance. There was nowhere to go. Ali’s city of Jilib was under attack. Repeated airstrikes, said the mother of six, were pinning its population beside the rising river. “The drones come all the time,” said the 27-year-old. “We hear them constantly. They kill animals, civilians. The town is big but destruction is everywhere.” Asho Omar from Malenda, a village near Jilib, described “constant” airstrikes that had forced people towards the banks of the Juba. “The airstrikes are everywhere; it is difficult to move. So many people have been killed.” Their testimony offers a rare glimpse of life inside the stronghold of al-Shabaab , the Islamist militants who control 30% of Somalia. items.headline: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
items.blurb: Maurene Comey believes she was let go from her job as a federal prosecutor because her father is the former FBI director.
items.text: The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled. Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations. Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay. A spokesperson for the justice department said in a statement that it disagreed with the decision and "will appeal in due course". In his ruling, Judge Furman said Comey's dismissal violated the US Constitution as well as her right to a fair legal process. He said the US attorney general can fire federal prosecutors but only "in a particular manner and only for certain reasons". Furman noted that in Comey's role, "she was assigned some of the country's highest profile cases and consistently received the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike". Comey

items.headline: US court rules against Trump administration in California voting case
items.blurb: US appeals court blocks government effort to stop California from tabulating ballots from list of alleged non-citizens.
items.text: A United States appeals court has ruled against the administration of President Donald Trump in its bid to block the state of California from counting certain mail-in ballots this election cycle. In a decision on Monday, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request from the government to sequester roughly 20,000 mailed ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm election. The Trump administration had asserted that the ballots were sent to people who are “likely” non-citizens. But it has not publicly revealed how it created its list or determined that the voters identified upon it were ineligible due to their citizenship status. In a two-to-one decision, the appeals court said the Trump administration had not given lower courts enough time to review the case. It therefore declined to stop California’s ballot tabulation. The court’s majority also underscored that election administration was the state’s responsibility under the US Constitution. The Trump administration was asking “the federal court to dictate to a state legislature a matter squarely within the state’s traditional domain”, Judge Gabriel Sanchez wrote in his opinion. Sanchez

items.headline: Sudan paramilitary drone strikes cause mass power cuts in eastern states
items.blurb: Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said.
items.text: Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said. The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref and one in White Nile state, “resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states”, the official said on condition of anonymity. All three states are controlled by the Sudanese army, which has been at war with the RSF, its former ally, since April 2023. The United Nations has repeatedly warned that regular attacks on power stations threaten health and services for millions of people who are already facing the world’s largest hunger crisis. Babiker Youssef, a resident of Al-Fao, in Gedaref, said the power had been out there since early morning. “My son is diabetic, his insulin has to be stored in the fridge,” he said over the phone, adding that he feared he would not be able to replace the medication

items.text: Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US. The firm's valuation is expected to exceed that of SpaceX, which was the biggest-ever listing at an initial valuation of about $1.8 trillion in the summer. Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, their price range, or a date for the listing. The Claude chatbot developer reported $16.3bn (£12.2bn) of revenue in the first half of the year, with losses of more than $80.7bn. Anthropic, which said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology. In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said concerns had been raised by policymakers, regulators and researchers as well as by people within its organisation that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity. items.headline: Centre clears E100 certification for flex-fuel vehicles
items.blurb: The change applies only to vehicles designed for high-ethanol fuels, not conventional petrol cars. Limited vehicle sales and fuel availability remain a hurdle.
items.text: The Centre on Monday cleared a key regulatory hurdle for vehicles capable of running on 100% ethanol (E100), formally recognising this category alongside those fuelled by 85% ethanol (E85) in vehicle emission certification provisions. The move comes amid nascent efforts to develop a market for flexi fuel vehicles -- those which can run on fuel with a high level of ethanol blending or petrol. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) notified amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, on October 23, published in the Gazette on October 26, replacing references to E85 with “E85 or E100” in specified emission-related provisions. The rules also specify that E85 or E100 can be used only in vehicles designed by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) as flex-fuel vehicles. The changes do not make either fuel suitable for conventional petrol vehicles, including those designed for E10 or E20. The roll-out of E20 petrol, which contains 20% ethanol, has seen motorists raise questions about fuel efficiency, compatibility with older vehicles and possible damage to engine components. Similarly, heavy vehicles travelling from Vyttila to Aluva must proceed towards Cheranalloor and take the North Paravur-Kodungallur road. All our state units will decide how they will counter the fake narrative being peddled by the Congress and other opposition parties against the Election Commission and SIR,” a senior BJP leader said. “There will be padyatras in some states, senior leaders including Union ministers will also address media briefings on the issue.” The leader added that CMs of BJP-ruled states and Union ministers are likely to participate in the programmes and marches to reach out to voters and explain the SIR exercise. items.blurb: A common affidavit filed for the EC, CEC Kumar and Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi say that any attempt to restrain the CEC’s functioning is contrary to the 2023 Act; asserts that Form 6 was not amended; West Bengal CEO’s officers filed appeals against inclusions
items.text: ECI’s affidavit said a media report on the inner frictions and alleged unilateral or authoritarian functioning of the CEC was hardly evidence in court. File | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma The Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners have filed a joint affidavit highlighting that any attempt to restrain the functioning of the CEC will be contrary to law. The nearly 250-page document filed in the top court late on Monday (October 26, 2026) said a CEC cannot be removed from office except in the manner and the grounds identical to ousting a Supreme Court judge. The affidavit said a media report on the inner frictions and alleged unilateral or authoritarian functioning of the CEC was hardly evidence in court. Petitions basing itself on media reports should not be even maintainable in court. Petitioners who have challenged the functioning of the CEC include the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and other INDIA bloc leaders. items.blurb: The Uttar Pradesh government must pay within a month or face 18% annual interest, the bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran ruled.
items.text: The Supreme Court on Monday awarded ₹ 6 lakh in compensation to a man who spent six years in jail as an undertrial before being acquitted in a murder case, holding the Uttar Pradesh police accountable for a probe that jeopardised his life and liberty and describing the case as “a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with”. A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said six years had been “erased from the life of a man on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures”, castigating the investigating and prosecuting agencies for failing to establish even the most basic facts of the alleged crime. Directing the state government to pay ₹ 6 lakh within a month, the court effectively awarded ₹ 1 lakh for every year the man spent in custody. items.blurb: One 97 Communications Ltd, the parent company that operates the brand Paytm, reported an over 10-fold rise in profit after tax to Rs 225 crore in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), from Rs 21 crore a year ago, on a reported basis, marking its sixth consecutive profitable quarter.
items.text: Paytm gained consumer UPI payment market share for the sixth consecutive quarter, with Paytm UPI transaction value growing 42 per cent for the quarter, more than double the industry growth rate of 19 per cent One 97 Communications Ltd, the parent company that operates the brand Paytm, reported an over 10-fold rise in profit after tax to ₹225 crore in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), from ₹21 crore a year ago, on a reported basis, marking its sixth consecutive profitable quarter. Operating revenue rose 28 per cent YoY to ₹2,648 crore, driven by sustained momentum across merchant and consumer businesses, expanded monetisation and AI adoption. Ebitda rose 90 per cent YoY to a record ₹270 crore, with Ebitda margin expanding to 10 per cent, reaching double digits for the first time and reflecting stronger operating profitability. For H1 FY27, profit after tax more than tripled YoY to ₹445 crore, from ₹144 crore a year ago, on a reported basis. On a comparable basis, excluding the Payments Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) incentive received until December 2025, underlying growth was even stronger.

items.headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
items.blurb: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark…
items.text: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores. Those advances have been extraordinary. But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?” Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability. For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it. There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem. A customer-facing assistant optimized for fast responses has fundamentally different requirements from a document-processing pipeline that can run overnight.

Five days after the spectacle, made possible by compressed-gas thrusters developed by Musk’s SpaceX, he revealed the companies were exploring a merger that could accelerate his push into autonomous driving. At stake is more than a technological race. Car groups, already grappling with growing Chinese competition, are seeking to move beyond a business model centered on vehicle sales towards one that also generates recurring revenues from software and AI-powered services. “Automakers are starting to look in the mirror and the software piece is what they are all looking at as the golden goose, because the margins are so high,” said Dan Ives, a tech analyst and partner at merchant bank Yorkville Ives. items.headline: Making the case for context-aware AI
items.blurb: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one.
items.text: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one. As companies look to move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, the challenge ahead is giving technology the context to act usefully within complex business processes. For Devavrat Shah, chief scientist of enterprise AI at Celonis, that context is central to what he calls “decision intelligence.” AI agents can support individual tasks within larger decision-making processes, he argues, but they need to understand the role each task plays and the business conditions surrounding it. “You can't just do that in a vacuum,” he says. Without the right operational context, agents risk overlooking important constraints, making costly mistakes, or consuming excessive computing resources as they try to work out what they need to know. items.text: Highway thieves are using sophisticated digital tactics that investigators worry make it easy to rob trucks carrying millions in expensive data center equipment. NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts yet and reported that since June, thieves have “made away with more than $100 million in data center freight.” Here’s how they said thieves get away with it: First, thieves hack freight brokers’ accounts on shipment-listing websites and post fake shipments to lure real bids, then send a malicious link to any trucking companies that respond. Once victims click, thieves install software to take control of their accounts and start bidding on real shipments. Sometimes, a real delivery driver is hired to collect the cargo, unaware of the scam, and other times fake driver’s licenses are used to get accomplices hired. Either way, the goods are eventually transferred to a driver working with the thieves to resell the gear, and, in one of the largest thefts, tracking coordinates were spoofed to prevent digital monitoring. items.headline: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
items.blurb: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide. A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl. These are important protections, and they should have existed all along.
items.text: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide . A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl . These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling. We have historically allowed the debate over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. As we transition into an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than merely address catastrophic harms. We should take measures to ensure that its products don’t erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another. items.headline: ICE plan to buy robot dogs spurs protest from hundreds of Boston Dynamics employees
items.blurb: US robotics company stands by ICE deal as more than 300 employees warn of risk.
items.text: Hundreds of employees at the US robotics firm Boston Dynamics signed a petition calling for executives to halt a sale of the company’s robot dogs to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement—but executives stood by the deal, while saying the robots would not be weaponized. On September 25, the Department of Homeland Security contract awarded $1.3 million to a Connecticut company called Radeco to provide ICE with modified versions of Boston Dynamics’ quadruped robots. After weeks of leaked S-1s , Anthropic finally filed for an initial public offering on Monday, setting the stage for one of the most closely watched public debuts in modern U.S. history. Anthropic, which plans to list under the ticker “ANT,” recorded revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion in the same period last year, according to the firm’s latest SEC filing. That revenue came off the back of an operating loss of $693 million, an improvement from the $2.1 billion in operating losses that Anthropic recorded in the first half of 2025. items.headline: Tata Communications To Pour Up To $450 Mn To Build AI Connectivity Infrastructure
items.blurb: Tata Communications plans to invest $400–450 Mn (around ₹4,350 Cr) to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India…
items.text: Tata Communications plans to invest ₹4,350 Cr in 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India The investment targets rising demand for low-latency connectivity as AI adoption, hyperscale data centres and cloud workloads expand The expansion will be rolled out in phases between FY30 and FY36, while E2E Networks separately plans to add 5.4 MW of AI compute capacity Tata Communications plans to invest $400–450 Mn (around ₹4,350 Cr) to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India in a bid to capitalise on rising demand for data centre connectivity and compute infrastructure. The investment will be used to build a new high-speed fibre network connecting major data centres and AI hubs, allowing transfer of large amounts of data faster with minimal delays. The network will also connect to Tata Communications’ existing global network . The company plans to add around 6 petabits per second (pbps) of network capacity under the programme, taking its total capacity to approximately 7.25 pbps once the expansion is completed.
